verses.32:9: And they went up to the Valley of the Cluster, and inspected the land, and turned away the heart of the children of Israel, so that they should not enter into the land which the Lord gave them.
verses.32:10: And the Lord was provoked to wrath on that day, and swore, saying,
verses.32:11: 'Surely none of these men who came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and above, who know evil and good, shall see the land which He swore to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob; for they have not wholly followed after Me,
verses.32:12: except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the one who was set apart, and Joshua the son of Nun, because they have wholly followed after the Lord.'
verses.32:13: And the Lord was provoked to wrath against Israel, and made them wander about in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation was consumed, those who did evil things before the Lord.
verses.32:14: Behold, you have risen up in place of your fathers, a band of sinful men, to add yet more to the fury of the wrath of the Lord against Israel;
verses.32:15: for you will turn away from Him, so as to leave them yet again in the wilderness, and you will act lawlessly against this whole congregation."
verses.32:16: And they came near to him and said, "Let us build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones;
verses.32:17: and we ourselves, armed as a vanguard, will go before the children of Israel, until we have brought them into their own place; and our little ones shall dwell in walled cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
verses.32:18: We will by no means return to our houses until the children of Israel have been apportioned each to his own inheritance.
verses.32:19: And we shall no longer inherit among them from across the Jordan and beyond, because we have received our portions on the other side of the Jordan toward the east."
verses.32:20: Then Moses said to them, "If you do according to this word, if you arm yourselves before the Lord for war,
verses.32:21: and every armed man of yours crosses over the Jordan before the Lord until His enemy is destroyed from before His face,
verses.32:22: and the land is subdued before the Lord, then afterward you shall return; and you shall be guiltless before the Lord and toward Israel, and this land shall be yours as a possession before the Lord.
verses.32:23: But if you do not do so, you will sin before the Lord, and you shall know your sin when evils overtake you.
verses.32:24: And you shall build for yourselves cities for your little ones and folds for your livestock; and that which proceeds from your mouth, this you shall do."
verses.32:25: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad spoke to Moses, saying, "Your servants will do just as our lord commands.
verses.32:26: Our little ones, and our wives, and all our livestock shall be in the cities of Gilead;
verses.32:27: but your servants will all cross over, armed and arrayed before the Lord for battle, just as our lord says."
verses.32:28: And Moses appointed over them Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the rulers of the fathers' houses of the tribes of Israel,
verses.32:29: and Moses said to them, "If the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad cross over the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the Lord, and you subdue the land before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession;
verses.32:30: but if they do not cross over armed with you to battle before the Lord, bring their little ones, and their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and they shall inherit together with you in the land of Canaan."
verses.32:31: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad answered, saying, "Whatever the Lord says to His servants, so we shall do;
verses.32:32: we will cross over armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and you shall give us the possession on the other side of the Jordan."
verses.32:33: So Moses gave to them—to the sons of Gad, and to the sons of Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh of the sons of Joseph—the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land and the cities with its borders, the cities of the land round about.
verses.32:34: And the sons of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer,
verses.32:35: and Sophar, and Jazer, and raised them up;
verses.32:36: and Namram, and Beth Haran, fortified cities and sheepfolds.
verses.32:37: And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
verses.32:38: and Baal Meon, encircled, and Sibmah; and they named the names of the cities which they built according to their own names.
verses.32:39: And the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, went to Gilead and took it, and destroyed the Amorite who dwelt in it.
verses.32:40: And Moses gave Gilead to Machir the son of Manasseh, and he dwelt there.
verses.32:41: And Jair the son of Manasseh went and took their settlements, and called them the Settlements of Jair.
verses.32:42: And Nobah went and took Kaath and its villages, and called them Naboth after his own name.
verses.33:1: And these are the stations of the children of Israel, as they went out from the land of Egypt with their host by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.33:2: And Moses wrote down their departures and their stations by the word of the Lord. And these are the stations of their journey.
verses.33:3: They departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the children of Israel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians,
verses.33:4: while the Egyptians were burying all the dead from among themselves whom the Lord had struck, every firstborn in the land of Egypt; and upon their gods the Lord executed vengeance.
verses.33:5: And the children of Israel, having departed from Rameses, encamped at Succoth.
verses.33:6: And they departed from Succoth and encamped at Buthan, which is a part of the wilderness.
verses.33:7: And they departed from Buthan and encamped by the mouth of Epiroth, which is opposite Baal Zephon, and they encamped opposite Migdol.
verses.33:8: And they departed from before Hiroth and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness; and they walked a journey of three days through the wilderness and encamped at Bitterness.
verses.33:9: And they departed from Bitterness and came to Elim; and at Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they encamped there by the water.
verses.33:10: And they departed from Elim and encamped by the Red Sea.
verses.33:11: And they departed from the Red Sea and encamped in the Wilderness of Sin.
verses.33:12: And they departed from the Wilderness of Sin and encamped at Raphaca.
verses.33:13: And they departed from Raphaca and encamped at Elim.
verses.33:14: And they departed from Elim and encamped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink there.
verses.33:15: And they departed from Rephidim and encamped in the Wilderness of Sinai.
verses.33:16: And they departed from the Wilderness of Sinai and encamped at Graves of Craving.
verses.33:17: And they departed from Graves of Craving and encamped at Hazeroth.
verses.33:18: And they departed from Hazeroth and encamped at Rithmah.
verses.33:19: And they departed from Rithmah and encamped at Rimmon Perez.
verses.33:20: And they departed from Rimmon Perez and encamped at Lemona.
verses.33:21: And they departed from Lemona and encamped at Dessa.
verses.33:22: And they departed from Dessa and encamped at Makellath.
verses.33:23: And they departed from Makellath and encamped at Shepher.
verses.33:24: And they departed from Shepher and encamped at Haradath.
verses.33:25: And they departed from Haradath and encamped at Makheloth.
verses.33:26: And they departed from Makheloth and encamped at Kataath.
verses.33:27: And they departed from Kataath and encamped at Tarath.
verses.33:28: And they departed from Tarath and encamped at Mithkah.
verses.33:29: And they departed from Mithkah and encamped at Zalmonah.
verses.33:30: And they departed from Zalmonah and encamped at Moseroth.
verses.33:31: And they departed from Moseroth and encamped at Banaia.
verses.33:32: And they departed from Banaia and encamped at Mount Gadgad.
verses.33:33: And they departed from Mount Gadgad and encamped at Setebatha.
verses.33:34: And they departed from Setebatha and encamped at Sebrona.
verses.33:35: And they departed from Sebrona and encamped at Ezion Geber.
verses.33:36: And they departed from Ezion Geber and encamped in the Wilderness of Zin; and they departed from the Wilderness of Zin and encamped in the Wilderness of Paran, that is, Kadesh.
verses.33:37: And they departed from Kadesh and encamped at Mount Hor, near the land of Edom.
verses.33:38: And Aaron the priest went up by the command of the Lord, and died there in the fortieth year of the departure of the children of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
verses.33:39: And Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
verses.33:40: And the Canaanite, king of Arad—and he dwelt in the land of Canaan—heard when the children of Israel were coming in.
verses.33:41: And they departed from Mount Hor and encamped at Zalmonah.
verses.33:42: And they departed from Zalmonah and encamped at Phino.
verses.33:43: And they departed from Phino and encamped at Soboth.
verses.33:44: And they departed from Soboth and encamped at Gai, on the far side, at the borders of Moab.
verses.33:45: And they departed from Gai and encamped at Dibon Gad.
verses.33:46: And they departed from Dibon Gad and encamped at Almon Diblathaim.
verses.33:47: And they departed from Almon Diblathaim and encamped upon the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
verses.33:48: And they departed from the mountains of Abarim and encamped on the west of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
verses.33:49: And they encamped by the Jordan between Aesimoth as far as Belsa, which is toward the west of Moab.
verses.33:50: And the Lord spoke to Moses on the west of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying,
verses.33:51: "Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan;
verses.33:52: and you shall destroy all those who dwell in the land from before your face, and you shall remove their watchtowers, and all their molten idols you shall destroy, and all their pillars you shall remove.
verses.33:53: And you shall destroy all those who dwell in the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given their land for an inheritance.
verses.33:54: And you shall divide their land for an inheritance by lot according to their tribes; to the larger you shall increase their possession, and to the smaller you shall diminish their possession; wherever his name goes forth, there it shall be his; according to the tribes of your families you shall inherit.
verses.33:55: But if you do not destroy those who dwell upon the land from before your face, then it shall be that those whom you leave of them shall be thorns in your eyes and darts in your sides, and they shall be hostile upon the land in which you shall dwell;
verses.33:56: and it shall come to pass that just as I had resolved to do to them, I will do to you.'"
verses.34:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:2: "Command the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You are entering into the land of Canaan; this shall be to you for the inheritance, the land of Canaan with its borders.
verses.34:3: And your side toward the south shall be from the wilderness of Zin extending alongside Edom, and your border toward the south shall be from the edge of the Salt Sea on the east;
verses.34:4: and the border shall turn around you from the south toward the Ascent of Akrabbim, and pass along to Ennak, and its outlet shall be to the south of Kadesh Barnea; then it shall go out to the village of Arad, and pass on to Azmon.
verses.34:5: And the border shall turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt, and the outlet shall be the sea.
verses.34:6: And you shall have the border of the sea: the Great Sea shall mark the boundary; this shall be to you the border of the sea.
verses.34:7: And this shall be your border toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure off for yourselves along the mountain, the mountain;
verses.34:8: and from the mountain, the mountain you shall measure off for them to the entrance of Hamath, and its outlet shall be the border of Saradak;
verses.34:9: and the border shall go out to Dephrona, and its outlet shall be Harsenaim; this shall be your border on the north.
verses.34:10: And you shall measure off for yourselves the eastern border from Harsenain to Sepphamar;
verses.34:11: and the border shall go down from Sepphamar to Bela on the east to the springs, and the border of Bela shall go down to the slope of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east.
verses.34:12: And the border shall go down to the Jordan, and the outlet shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its borders all around.'"
verses.34:13: Then Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying, "This is the land which you shall inherit by lot, just as the Lord commanded Moses to give it to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe of Manasseh;
verses.34:14: for the tribe of the sons of Reuben and the tribe of the sons of Gad, according to their fathers' houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their portions.
verses.34:15: Two tribes and a half-tribe have received their portions beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, on the south toward the east."
verses.34:16: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:17: "These are the names of the men who shall apportion the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.34:18: And you shall take one leader from each tribe to apportion the land to you as an inheritance.
verses.34:19: And these are the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh;
verses.34:20: of the tribe of Simeon, Salamiel the son of Semiud;
verses.34:21: of the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad the son of Chislon;
verses.34:22: of the tribe of Dan, a leader, Bakchir the son of Jogli;
verses.34:23: of the sons of Joseph, of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, a leader, Hanniel the son of Suphi;
verses.34:24: of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, a leader, Kemuel the son of Sabatha;
verses.34:25: of the tribe of Zebulun, a leader, Elizaphan the son of Parnach;
verses.34:26: of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, a leader, Paltiel the son of Oza;
verses.34:27: of the tribe of the sons of Asher, a leader, Achior the son of Shelomi;
verses.34:28: of the tribe of Naphtali, a leader, Pedahel the son of Beniamiud."
verses.34:29: These are the ones whom the Lord commanded to make the apportionment for the children of Israel in the land of Canaan.
verses.35:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses on the west of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying,
verses.35:2: "Command the children of Israel, and they shall give to the Levites from the portions of their possession cities to dwell in; and the outskirts of the cities around them they shall give to the Levites.
verses.35:3: And the cities shall be theirs to dwell in, and their set-apart grounds shall be for their cattle and for all their four-footed beasts.
verses.35:4: And the adjoining lands of the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall extend from the wall of the city and outward two thousand cubits all around.
verses.35:5: And you shall measure outside the city on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the side toward the sea two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits; and the city in the midst of this shall be yours, and the bordering lands of the cities.
verses.35:6: And the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall give for the manslayer to flee there, and in addition to these, forty-two cities.
verses.35:7: All the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, these and their outskirts.
verses.35:8: And as for the cities which you shall give from the possession of the children of Israel, from those who have many you shall give many, and from those who have fewer, fewer; each according to his inheritance which they shall inherit, they shall give of the cities to the Levites."
verses.35:9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.35:10: "Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.35:11: and you shall set apart cities for yourselves; they shall be places of refuge for you, that the manslayer may flee there, everyone who strikes a person unintentionally.
verses.35:12: And the cities shall be places of refuge for you from the avenger of blood, so that the manslayer shall by no means die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
verses.35:13: And the cities which you shall give, the six cities, shall be places of refuge for you:
verses.35:14: three cities you shall give beyond the Jordan, and the three cities you shall give in the land of Canaan.
verses.35:15: There shall be a refuge for the children of Israel, and for the proselyte who sojourns among you; these cities shall be for a place of refuge, for everyone who strikes a person unintentionally to flee there.
verses.35:16: But if he strikes him with an instrument of iron so that he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:17: And if he strikes him with a stone in the hand by which one may die, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:18: And if he strikes him with a wooden instrument in the hand by which one may die, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:19: The avenger of blood himself shall slay the murderer; whenever he meets him, he himself shall slay him.
verses.35:20: And if out of hatred he pushes him and hurls any object upon him from ambush, so that he dies,
verses.35:21: or in wrath he struck him with his hand, so that he dies, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death. The avenger of blood shall slay the murderer when he meets him.
verses.35:22: But if suddenly, not out of hatred, he pushes him, or hurls any object upon him without ambush,
verses.35:23: or with any stone by which one may die, without knowing, and it falls upon him so that he dies, while he was not his enemy nor seeking to do him harm,
verses.35:24: then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the avenger of blood according to these judgments.
verses.35:25: And the congregation shall deliver the manslayer from the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge to which he had fled; and he shall dwell there until the high priest dies, whom they anointed with the holy oil.
verses.35:26: But if the manslayer at all goes outside the borders of the city to which he fled,
verses.35:27: and the avenger of blood finds him outside the borders of the city of his refuge, and the avenger of blood slays the manslayer, he is not guilty;
verses.35:28: for he shall dwell in the city of refuge until the high priest dies; after the death of the high priest, the manslayer shall return to the land of his possession.
verses.35:29: And these things shall be to you for a statute of judgment throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.35:30: Whoever strikes a person, by witnesses you shall slay the murderer; and one witness shall not testify against a person so that he should die.
verses.35:31: And you shall not accept a ransom for the life from the murderer who is liable to be put to death, for he shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:32: You shall not accept a ransom for fleeing to a city of refuge, to dwell again upon the land, until the high priest dies.
verses.35:33: And you shall by no means stain with murder the land in which you dwell, for this blood stains the land with murder; and atonement shall not be made for the land for the blood that was shed upon it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
verses.35:34: And you shall not defile the land on which you dwell, upon which I will dwell among you; for I am the Lord who dwells in the midst of the children of Israel.'"
verses.36:1: And the leaders of the tribe of the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from the tribe of the sons of Joseph, came near and spoke before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders of the fathers' houses of the sons of Israel.
verses.36:2: And they said, "The Lord commanded our lord to assign the land of the inheritance by lot to the sons of Israel, and the Lord directed our lord to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.
verses.36:3: And they will become wives to one from the tribes of the sons of Israel, and their lot will be taken away from the possession of our fathers, and it will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to whom they may become wives, and from the lot of our inheritance it will be taken away.
verses.36:4: And when the release of the sons of Israel comes, then their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to whom they may become wives, and from the inheritance of the tribe of our lineage their inheritance will be taken away."
verses.36:5: And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the ordinance of the Lord, saying, "Thus the tribe of the sons of Joseph speak.
verses.36:6: This is the word which the Lord has directed for the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, 'Where it is pleasing in their sight, let them become wives; only from the clan of their father let them become wives.'
verses.36:7: And no inheritance of the sons of Israel shall be transferred from tribe to tribe, for the sons of Israel shall each cleave to the inheritance of the tribe of his lineage.
verses.36:8: And every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the sons of Israel shall become a wife to one of those from the clan of her father, so that the sons of Israel may each possess his paternal inheritance.
verses.36:9: And no lot shall be transferred from one tribe to another tribe, but the sons of Israel shall each cleave to his own inheritance."
verses.36:10: Just as the Lord directed Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.
verses.36:11: And Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married to their cousins.
verses.36:12: From the clan of Manasseh, of the sons of Joseph, they became wives, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of the clan of their father.
verses.36:13: These are the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses on the west of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.

notes.1:14: The Greek reads "Reuel" (Rhagouel, agreeing with Numbers 2:14), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Deuel" in this verse.
notes.1:18: The Greek reads "on the first day of the month of the second year" and uses the rare verb epexonousan (literally "enrolled on tablets" or "registered by lineage"), rendered "registered them."
notes.1:24: In the Greek text, Judah is listed third here (vv. 24-25) and Gad is placed ninth after Benjamin (vv. 36-37), differing from the order in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:33: The Greek text reads "thirty-two thousand three hundred" (triakosioi), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "thirty-two thousand two hundred."
notes.1:53: The Greek includes "before the Lord" and reads "there shall be no sin" (hamartema), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "wrath."
notes.2:2: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew phrase "tent of meeting" as "tabernacle of the testimony" (skene tou martyriou) and translates Hebrew degel ("standard") as tagma ("division").
notes.2:3: The Greek reads "toward the south, toward the east" (kata noton kat' anatolas), a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "eastward, toward the sunrise."
notes.2:18: "By the sea" (para thalassan) is the literal Greek rendering of the directional idiom for westward, looking toward the Mediterranean Sea.
notes.2:21: The Septuagint numbers Manasseh at thirty-two thousand four hundred, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads thirty-two thousand two hundred, though the camp subtotal in verse 24 remains one hundred eight thousand one hundred.
notes.2:26: The Septuagint numbers Dan at sixty-two thousand five hundred, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads sixty-two thousand seven hundred; this offsets the extra two hundred in Manasseh (verse 21), preserving the overall total of six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty in verse 32.
notes.3:2: The Greek reads Abiud here and in verse 4, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Abihu.
notes.3:10: The Septuagint includes the fuller phrases "over the tabernacle of the testimony" and "all things concerning the altar and within the veil," and reads "who touches" where the Hebrew reads "who draws near."
notes.3:17: The Greek reads Gedson here and throughout the chapter (as well as Dael in verse 24), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Gershon (and Lael in verse 24).
notes.3:34: The Greek gives the number of the Merarites as six thousand fifty, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads six thousand two hundred.
notes.3:47: The Greek uses Hellenistic coinage terms here, rendering the sanctuary standard as "the holy didrachm" (compare "the holy shekel" in verse 50) and the smaller unit as "obols."
notes.4:3: The Greek text gives the Levitical service age as twenty-five to fifty years old throughout this chapter (compare Numbers 8:24), whereas the Masoretic Text reads thirty to fifty.
notes.4:6: Greek hyakinthinon ("blue" or "hyacinth-blue") describes both the inner cloth and the outer leather covering across verses 6 through 14; in verse 7 the Greek also specifies a cloth wholly of purple for the table, where the Masoretic Text reads blue.
notes.4:13: The Greek reads "he shall place the cover upon the altar" (echoing "the cover" in verse 14), whereas the Masoretic Text directs that they remove the ashes from the altar.
notes.4:14: The closing instruction concerning the covering and transport of the laver and its base is preserved in the Septuagint (and Samaritan Pentateuch) but does not appear in the Masoretic Text.
notes.4:36: The Greek text numbers the Kohathites at two thousand two hundred and fifty (compared to two thousand seven hundred and fifty in the Masoretic Text), while the combined Levitical total in verse 48 remains eight thousand five hundred and eighty.
notes.5:2: The Greek phrase rendered "because of a dead body" is literally "upon a soul," a Septuagint idiom for ritual defilement caused by a corpse.
notes.5:17: The Septuagint specifies "pure living water," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "holy water."
notes.5:18: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of "bitter water," the Septuagint reads "water of conviction," emphasizing legal exposure and proof of guilt.
notes.6:2: Rather than transliterating the Hebrew term "Nazirite," the Septuagint translates it throughout this chapter as making a vow of consecration or purity to the Lord.
notes.6:11: The Septuagint includes the clause "on which he was consecrated to the Lord for the days of the vow" at the end of verse 11, rather than beginning verse 12 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.6:23: The Septuagint places the promise about placing God's name on Israel here before the priestly blessing and includes "the Lord," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text places it after the blessing as verse 27.
notes.6:25: The Septuagint begins this line with "and" and renders the verb as "have mercy upon you" rather than "be gracious to you."
notes.7:2: The Greek explicitly specifies "twelve rulers" (absent in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and uses episkope ("inspection" or "oversight") for the census administration.
notes.7:17: The Greek thysia soteriu ("sacrifice of deliverance") corresponds to the Hebrew peace offering, and uniquely specifies feminine animals—two heifers (damaleis) and five year-old ewe lambs (amnadas)—throughout the chapter's offerings.
notes.7:29: Following the Greek critical text, "five male goats" is omitted in both 7:29 and 7:41, though present in the other days' offering lists.
notes.7:30: The Greek text reads Edisur here, whereas 7:35 reads Sediur (Shedeur).
notes.7:42: The Greek text reads Raguel (Reuel), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Deuel here.
notes.7:84: The Greek reads "from the sons of Israel," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from the leaders of Israel."
notes.7:86: The Greek omits the phrase "ten shekels apiece, according to the shekel of the sanctuary," which appears in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:87: The Greek explicitly adds "and their drink offerings" alongside the sacrifices, a clause not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:88: The Greek adds "without blemish" to the sixty year-old ewe lambs and concludes with "after filling his hands and after anointing him" (reflecting the idiom for priestly consecration with a masculine pronoun), whereas the Hebrew reads "after it was anointed."
notes.7:89: The Greek explicitly specifies "the voice of the Lord" speaking from above the mercy seat, whereas the Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed.
notes.8:8: The Greek specifies "a year-old calf" (μόσχον ἐνιαύσιον) for the sin offering, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a second young bull."
notes.8:11: Throughout this passage (vv. 11, 13, 16, 19, 21), the Septuagint renders the Hebrew wave-offering terminology as setting apart or presenting the Levites as a "gift" (ἀπόδομα) before the Lord.
notes.8:19: The Greek reads "there shall not be among the sons of Israel anyone drawing near to the holy things" (προσεγγίζων πρὸς τὰ ἅγια), without the Masoretic Text's reference to a plague.
notes.8:26: The Greek makes "his brother" (ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ) the nominative subject who ministers in the tabernacle of the testimony, whereas the Masoretic Text states that the retired Levite may assist his brothers.
notes.9:4: The Greek places the temporal clause with the unusual participle "beginning" (ἐναρχομένου) in verse 4, omitting the fuller statement of observance found in verse 5 of the Masoretic Text.
notes.9:6: Literally "on account of a soul of a man" (ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου), the standard Septuagint idiom for ritual defilement through contact with a human corpse (similarly in vv. 7, 10).
notes.9:18: From verse 18 through verse 23, the Septuagint casts the Israelites' responses to the cloud in the future tense ("shall encamp," "shall set out") and places encampment before departure in verse 18.
notes.9:22: The Greek reads simply "for a month, or a day" (μηνός, ἡμέρας), differing from the Masoretic Text's "two days, or a month, or a year," and omits the closing clause about departing when the cloud lifted.
notes.10:6: The Greek text preserves trumpet alarms for all four cardinal directions (east, south, west by the sea, and north), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions only the east and south.
notes.10:17: Here and in verses 21, 22, and 25, the Greek shifts from past narrative verbs to the future tense ("shall take down," "shall set out"), reflecting the prescribed marching order.
notes.10:31: The Greek reads "because you were with us in the wilderness, and you shall be an elder among us," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "since you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you shall be eyes for us."
notes.10:34: In the Greek text, Moses's prayers at the ark's setting out and resting appear in verses 34-35, followed by the cloud shading the camp in verse 36 (reversing the Hebrew Masoretic order of verses 34 and 35-36).
notes.11:3: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Taberah as Enpyrismos ("Burning").
notes.11:7: The Greek describes the manna's appearance as "crystal" (krystallos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text compares it to bdellium.
notes.11:28: The Greek identifies Joshua as "the chosen one" (eklektos), reading the underlying Hebrew differently from the Masoretic Text's "from his youth."
notes.11:32: The Greek reads "slaughtered them to dry for themselves" (esphaxan... psygmous) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "spread them out"; a "cor" (Greek koros) is a dry measure equivalent to a homer.
notes.11:34: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Kibroth Hattaavah as Mnemata tes epithymias ("Graves of Craving").
notes.12:1: The Septuagint identifies Moses' wife as an Ethiopian woman (Aithiopissa) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Cushite.
notes.12:6: The Greek links "for the Lord" (Kyrio) to "a prophet of yours" and reads "in sleep" (en hypno) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "in a dream."
notes.12:8: The Septuagint reads "the glory of the Lord" (ten doxan Kyriou) with an aorist verb ("has beheld") rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "form" or "likeness."
notes.12:15: The Septuagint reads "until Miriam was cleansed" (ekatharisthe) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "until Miriam was brought in again."
notes.13:4: Several names in verses 4-15 reflect distinct Greek forms compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text: Samuel (13:4, MT Shammua), Suri (13:5, MT Hori), Ilaal (13:7, MT Igal), Gudiel in both 13:10 and 13:15 (MT Gaddiel and Geuel), Gamai (13:12, MT Gemalli), and Jabi (13:14, MT Vophsi).
notes.13:21: The Greek text reads "Ephaath" (Ephaath) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Hamath."
notes.13:22: The Septuagint uses the Greek geographical name "Tanis" (Tanin) for the Egyptian city called "Zoan" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:23: The Greek translates Eshcol as "Valley of the Cluster" (Pharanx botryos) and reads "cucumbers" (sikyōn, an ancient Septuagint reading) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "figs."
notes.13:32: The Greek reads "dismay" (ekstasin) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a bad report," and in 13:33 it repeats "before them" twice rather than contrasting "in our own sight" with "in their sight."
notes.14:3: Following the Septuagint verse division, the opening wish begins verse three rather than concluding verse two, and the Greek reads "to fall in war" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "by the sword."
notes.14:9: The Septuagint reads "the season" (or appointed time) has departed from them, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "their protection" (literally, "their shade").
notes.14:23: The Septuagint includes an extensive promise not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, granting the land to the children present who do not know good or evil, echoing Deuteronomy 1:39.
notes.14:27: The Septuagint reads that Israel murmured "concerning you" (referring to Moses and Aaron), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "against Me."
notes.14:34: The Septuagint renders the final phrase as "the fury of My wrath," translating a rare Hebrew noun often understood as "My opposition" or "My displeasure."
notes.15:3: The Greek reads "to magnify a vow" (also in 15:8), rendering the Hebrew idiom for fulfilling a special vow, and uses "burnt offerings" where the Masoretic Text has "an offering made by fire."
notes.15:10: Following the Greek critical text, this verse omits the clause specifying half a hin of wine for the drink offering that appears in the Masoretic Text and some manuscripts.
notes.15:14: The Greek places "the congregation" at the close of verse 14 ("so shall the congregation do to the Lord") rather than at the opening of verse 15 as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.15:30: The Greek reads "with a hand of arrogance" and "provokes God," corresponding to "with a high hand" and "blasphemes the LORD" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.15:39: In the Greek verse division, "so that you may remember and perform all My commandments" concludes verse 39 rather than beginning verse 40, and Greek "thoughts" corresponds to "heart" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.16:1: The Greek text reads "spoke" rather than the Hebrew "took," presenting Korah and his companions as initiating their challenge through speech.
notes.16:5: The Greek renders the Hebrew consonants for "in the morning" as a verb, yielding "God has examined and knows those who are His," phrasing later echoed in 2 Timothy 2:19.
notes.16:13: Unlike the Hebrew ("out of a land"), the Greek reads "into a land flowing with milk and honey," and continues in v. 14 with a contrafactual clause ("Even if you had brought us...").
notes.16:15: The Greek reads "anything desirable" (epithymema) where the Hebrew reads "a single donkey," reflecting a difference between similar Hebrew roots.
notes.16:26: The Greek text here reads "your belongings" (apartia hymon) rather than the variant "their sin" (hamartia auton), warning the congregation not to perish with all their possessions.
notes.17:1: In the Septuagint, chapter 17 opens with the bronze censers and the plague (vv. 1-15, corresponding to 16:36-50 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) before continuing with Aaron's rod (vv. 16-28, corresponding to 17:1-13 MT).
notes.17:7: The Greek uses a proleptic feminine demonstrative (tende, "this one") referring back to the tabernacle of testimony ahead of the resumptive pronoun "it."
notes.17:19: The Greek reads "I will be made known to you" (reflecting the Hebrew root "to know") where the Masoretic Text has "I will meet with you."
notes.17:23: The Greek uses the general term karya ("nuts") for the fruit yielded by Aaron's rod, corresponding to "almonds" in the Hebrew text.
notes.18:1: Greek reads "shall receive the firstfruits of the holy things" (τὰς ἀπαρχὰς τῶν ἁγίων), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary."
notes.18:8: Greek γέρας means a "gift of honor" or privileged portion, rendering the Hebrew term for a consecrated/anointed share.
notes.18:16: Greek renders the Hebrew weight gerah with ὀβολοί ("obols"), a Greek coin unit here valued at twenty to the holy shekel.
notes.18:28: Greek includes the pronoun αὐτούς ("them") before "you yourselves" and omits "of the Lord" before "a contribution to Aaron the priest."
notes.19:3: Greek adds "to a clean place" (εἰς τόπον καθαρόν) and uses plural verbs ("they shall bring her forth... they shall slaughter her"), as also in verse 6 ("they shall cast").
notes.19:14: Greek consistently renders "house" (οἰκία here and οἶκος in verse 18) where the Masoretic Hebrew has "tent."
notes.19:19: Greek reads "and he shall be unclean until evening" (ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται ἕως ἑσπέρας), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "and he shall be clean at evening."
notes.20:13: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew place name Meribah as "Contradiction" (Greek antilogia) here, and renders it as "Reviling" (Greek loidoria) in 20:24.
notes.20:19: The Septuagint reads "along by the mountain" twice, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "by the highway" and then "on foot."
notes.20:24: The Septuagint uses the second-person plural ("you shall by no means enter"), addressing both Moses and Aaron, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses the third-person singular ("he shall not enter").
notes.21:3: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew place name Hormah as "Anathema," signifying something devoted to destruction.
notes.21:11: "Chalgaei on the other side" preserves the Septuagint's distinct proper name (Chalgaei) corresponding to the Hebrew Iye-abarim.
notes.21:14: "He set Zoob ablaze" preserves the Septuagint's distinct proper name (Zoob) and verbal rendering of a difficult poetic line (Hebrew Masoretic Text: "Waheb in Suphah").
notes.21:18: The Septuagint renders the Song of the Well as "kings of the nations hewed it out, in their reign, when they held dominion" (Masoretic Text: "nobles of the people, with the scepter and with their staffs"). Verse 21:19 is merged into 21:20 in the Greek text, which preserves the distinct Septuagint names Manthanain, Manael, and Janen (for Hebrew Mattanah, Nahaliel, and "the valley") along with "the hewn height" for Pisgah.
notes.21:24: The Septuagint reads "Jazer" as the border of the sons of Ammon where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "strong." Likewise, in 21:26 the Septuagint reads "from Aroer" (Masoretic Text: "from his hand"), and in 21:30 it reads "the women have yet further kindled a fire against Moab."
notes.22:1: The Septuagint reads "on the west of Moab" (taking the Hebrew term for "plains" in the sense of "west/evening") rather than "in the plains of Moab."
notes.22:30: The Greek idiom literally reads "disregarding with disregard," rendering the Hebrew phrase for being accustomed to act in a certain way as acting with disdainful disregard.
notes.22:39: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Kiriath-huzoth literally as "Cities of Villages" (Poleis epayleon).
notes.22:41: The Septuagint reads "the pillar of Baal" rather than the Hebrew "Bamoth-baal" ("high places of Baal"), and explicitly states that Balak showed Balaam a part of the people.
notes.23:6: The Septuagint adds "And the Spirit of God came upon him" before Balaam's first oracle, paralleling Numbers 24:2.
notes.23:10: The Septuagint reads "seed" in both halves of the verse—corresponding to "dust" and "end" in the Hebrew—and translates the Hebrew "fourth part" as "peoples."
notes.23:14: The Greek translates the place name Pisgah literally as "the Hewn Rock" (Lelaxeumenou, from a verb meaning to hew stone).
notes.23:19: The Greek renders the parallel infinitives passively as "to be deceived" and "to be threatened," in contrast to the Hebrew "to lie" and "to relent."
notes.23:22: "Unicorn" translates the Greek monokerotos ("one-horned beast"), the standard Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew re'em ("wild ox").
notes.24:7: The Septuagint introduces a personal figure ("a man shall come forth from his seed") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of water flowing from buckets, and reads "Gog" rather than "Agag."
notes.24:17: The Septuagint reads "I will show to him" and "I call blessed" (MT: "I see him... I behold him") and renders Hebrew "scepter" as "a man" ("a man shall arise out of Israel"), highlighting the messianic character of the oracle.
notes.24:22: The Septuagint reads the Hebrew phrase for being consumed or burned as the proper name "Beor" and translates the clause as "a nest of craftiness."
notes.24:23: The Septuagint explicitly includes the name "Og" ("And seeing Og"), which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.24:24: The Septuagint reads "the Hebrews" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Eber," and has a singular verb ("shall come forth") from "the hand of the Kittim."
notes.25:1: The Septuagint reads "were profaned," reflecting a different sense of the Hebrew verb root than the Masoretic Text's "began."
notes.25:6: The Septuagint literally reads "brought his brother to the Midianite woman," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "brought to his brethren a Midianite woman."
notes.25:8: The Greek word translated "vaulted chamber" literally denotes a domed furnace or kiln, used here for a vaulted alcove or tent-chamber.
notes.25:14: The Septuagint gives the father's name as "Salmon," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Salu."
notes.25:15: The Septuagint treats the Hebrew plural noun for "peoples" or "tribes" as the proper name "Ommoth."
notes.26:3: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for plains as the place name Araboth ("Araboth of Moab"). In 26:4, the Greek also uniquely includes "you" ("you and the sons of Israel") in the direct address.
notes.26:15: In the Septuagint census, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun are listed before Gad and Asher, differing from the tribal order in the Hebrew Masoretic Text. The Greek also preserves distinct clan names here: Jamun in 26:17 (Hebrew Hamul) and Samaram in 26:20 (Hebrew Shimron).
notes.26:25: For Gad's clans, the Greek reads Addi (Hebrew Eri) and in 26:26 reads Ariel (Hebrew Areli). In 26:27, the Greek census total for Gad is 44,500, compared with 40,500 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:30: The Greek names Asher's daughter Kara, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Serah. Earlier in Asher's list, the Greek reads Jamin in 26:28 (Hebrew Jimnah) and Melliel in 26:29 (Hebrew Malchiel), without the Masoretic subheading introducing Heber and Malchiel as sons of Beriah.
notes.26:31: The Greek text gives Asher's total as 43,600 (using the Greek alphabetic numeral chi with keraia for 600), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text (26:47) records 53,400.
notes.26:39: The Greek lists two sons of Ephraim—Shuthelah and Tanach (Hebrew Tahan)—omitting Becher, and reads Eden in 26:40 (Hebrew Eran). Earlier in Manasseh's list, the Greek also reads Ahiezer in 26:34 (Hebrew Iezer) and Symaer in 26:36 (Hebrew Shemida).
notes.26:45: The Greek gives Benjamin's census total as 35,500, compared with 45,600 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text. In 26:42-44, the Greek also omits Hupham and reads Jachiran (Hebrew Ahiram), Adar (Hebrew Ard), and Noemani (Hebrew Naaman).
notes.26:47: For Dan, the Greek reads the clan name Shami (Hebrew Shuham) and records a total of 64,600 (using the Greek alphabetic numeral chi with keraia for 600), compared with 64,400 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:50: The Greek text records Naphtali's total as 30,300, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 45,400. In 26:48, the Greek also reads Sael where the Hebrew reads Jahzeel.
notes.26:59: The Greek reads actively "who bore these to Levi in Egypt," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads passively "who was born to Levi in Egypt." In 26:58, the Greek also omits the family of the Mahlites.
notes.27:3: The Greek text includes the petition traditionally numbered as verse 4 directly within verse 3, leaving no separate verse 4.
notes.27:7: The Greek text repeats the clause "and you shall speak to the sons of Israel" across the boundary of verses 7 and 8.
notes.27:12: Where the Hebrew text reads "Mount Abarim," the Greek renders the phrase as "the mountain that is in the region beyond" and explicitly identifies it as "this Mount Nebo."
notes.27:16: The Greek text reads "of the spirits and of all flesh," including "and" between the two phrases.
notes.27:21: Greek "ton delon" ("the Manifestations" or "the Clear Signs") translates the Hebrew Urim, and the Greek uses a plural verb ("they shall inquire of him").
notes.28:2: The Greek text enumerates three terms ("My offerings, My gifts, My offerings made by fire") and concludes with "at My feasts" rather than "at its appointed time."
notes.28:26: Greek "te hemera ton neon" ("the day of the new produce") corresponds to the Feast of Firstfruits, also called the Feast of Weeks.
notes.28:30: The Greek text splits the phrase "the continual burnt offering" ("tou holokautomatos tou dia pantos") across the boundary between verses 30 and 31.
notes.29:1: Greek hemera semasias literally means "a day of signaling," referring to the ceremonial sounding of trumpets on the first day of the seventh month.
notes.29:6: Greek synkrisis (translated "ordinance" throughout this chapter) is the Septuagint rendering for the prescribed ritual regulation or standard.
notes.29:11: The Greek text includes "to make atonement for you" and concludes with "according to the ordinance, for a sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to the Lord," where the Hebrew tradition is shorter.
notes.29:35: Greek exodion denotes a solemn closing festival or assembly concluding the seven-day Feast of Tabernacles.
notes.29:39: Greek soteria literally means "offerings of deliverance" (or "salvation offerings"), the Septuagint equivalent for peace or fellowship offerings.
notes.30:1: Following the Septuagint division, this verse opens chapter 30, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text and many English Bibles number it as 29:40.
notes.30:6: Greek kathariei (also in vv. 9 and 13) literally means "shall cleanse" or "clear," signifying that the Lord absolves the woman from obligation rather than the Hebrew "forgive."
notes.30:16: The Greek text reads ten hamartian autou ("his sin"), attributing the guilt to the husband who annuls the vow after the day he heard it, whereas the Hebrew reads "her iniquity."
notes.31:8: The Greek reads Robok for the fifth Midianite king, where the Hebrew text reads Reba, and adds "along with their slain" after the slaying of Balaam.
notes.31:12: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew expression for "the plains of Moab" as the place name Araboth of Moab.
notes.31:28: The Greek lists five categories here—people, livestock, oxen, sheep, and goats—whereas the Hebrew text omits livestock and has donkeys rather than goats.
notes.31:36: The Greek text reads three hundred and thirty-five thousand five hundred sheep here, whereas verse forty-three and the Hebrew text read three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred.
notes.31:54: The Greek renders the Hebrew "tent of meeting" as "tabernacle of testimony," the standard Septuagint designation throughout Numbers.
notes.32:11: The Septuagint includes the additional clause "who know evil and good" (cf. Deuteronomy 1:39), absent from the Masoretic Text, and shifts from third-person "He swore" to first-person "after Me."
notes.32:12: Where the Masoretic Text calls Caleb "the Kenizzite," the Septuagint translates the epithet as "the one who was set apart."
notes.32:23: The Septuagint reads "you shall know your sin when evils overtake you," in contrast to the Masoretic Text's "be sure your sin will find you out."
notes.32:30: The Septuagint includes an expanded command to bring their little ones, wives, and livestock across ahead of the Israelites into Canaan, which is not in the Masoretic Text.
notes.32:35: The Septuagint reads "Sophar" (for Hebrew "Atroth Shophan") and translates the Hebrew place name "Jogbehah" (from a root meaning "to be high") as the verb phrase "and raised them up"; distinct Septuagint proper-name forms also appear in vv. 36 (Namram) and 42 (Kaath, Naboth).
notes.33:6: The Greek text preserves several distinct place names across this itinerary compared with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, including Buthan (v. 6, for Etham), the mouth of Epiroth and Hiroth (vv. 7–8, translating Pi- as 'mouth'), Raphaca (v. 12), Elim (v. 13, for Alush), Lemona (v. 20), Dessa (v. 21), Makellath (v. 22), Kataath (v. 26), Zalmonah (v. 29, for Hashmonah), Banaia (v. 31), Setebatha (v. 33), Sebrona (v. 34), Phino (v. 42), Soboth (v. 43), Gai on the far side (v. 44), and Aesimoth to Belsa (v. 49).
notes.33:8: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Marah literally as Pikriai ('Bitterness'), and similarly renders Kibroth Hattaavah in verses 16–17 as Mnemasin epithymias ('Graves of Craving').
notes.33:36: The Septuagint records an extra stage here, distinguishing the encampment in the Wilderness of Zin from a further departure and encampment in the Wilderness of Paran, which is Kadesh.
notes.33:48: Literally 'on the west of Moab' (also in vv. 49–50), where the Greek interprets the Hebrew word for plains or steppes by the related term for evening or west.
notes.33:52: The Greek uses 'destroy' (also in vv. 53, 55) rather than 'drive out,' and renders the Canaanite cultic sites as 'watchtowers' and 'pillars.'
notes.34:4: The Greek text reads Ennak (where the Hebrew has Zin) and translates Hebrew hazar as a common noun while reading Arad, yielding "the village of Arad" (where the Hebrew has Hazar-addar).
notes.34:7: Here and in v. 8 the Greek renders Hebrew Hor ha-har ("Mount Hor") literally twice as "the mountain, the mountain" (to oros to oros).
notes.34:11: In vv. 8–11 the Greek preserves several distinct border place names compared with the Hebrew, including Saradak (for Zedad), Dephrona (for Ziphron), Harsenaim/Harsenain (for Hazar-enan), Sepphamar (for Shepham), and Bela (for Riblah), and translates Hebrew Ain as "the springs."
notes.34:15: The Greek reads "on the south toward the east" (apo notou kat' anatolas), where the Hebrew reads "eastward toward the sunrise."
notes.34:20: In vv. 20–28 the Greek preserves several distinct forms of the tribal leaders' and fathers' names compared with the Hebrew: Salamiel son of Semiud, Eldad, Bakchir, Suphi, Sabatha, Oza, Achior, and Beniamiud.
notes.35:1: The Greek reads "on the west of Moab" (epi dysmon Moab), reflecting a reading of Hebrew aravot ("plains") in connection with erev ("evening/west").
notes.35:4: The Greek specifies "two thousand cubits" here (matching v. 5), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "one thousand cubits."
notes.35:12: "The avenger of blood" translates Greek ho anchisteuon to haima, literally "the next of kin for the blood."
notes.35:32: The Greek uses an infinitive construction ("for fleeing to a city of refuge"), whereas the Hebrew refers to the person "who has fled to his city of refuge."
notes.35:33: "Stain with murder" renders the rare Septuagint verb phonoktoneo ("defile with murder/bloodshed"), where the Hebrew uses a verb meaning "pollute" or "defile."
notes.36:4: Greek aphesis ("release") is the Septuagint's standard rendering for the Year of Jubilee (cf. Leviticus 25:10).
notes.36:5: Greek houtos ("Thus") renders the underlying Hebrew ken literally in its adverbial sense rather than "rightly."
notes.36:8: The Greek verb anchisteuo ("possess") specifically denotes inheriting or succeeding to property by right of kinship as next of kin.
notes.36:11: The Septuagint places Mahlah last in the list of Zelophehad's daughters (rather than first as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and renders "sons of their uncles" concisely as anepsiois ("cousins").
notes.36:13: The Septuagint lists three legal terms ("commandments and the ordinances and the judgments") and renders the geography as epi dysmon Moab ("on the west of Moab"), reflecting an association of Hebrew arvot ("plains") with erev ("evening/west").
